meta.scope: Argentina batch 1 — Phase 0+1 complete. Core national statistical system from INDEC catalogue top-down: foundational law (Ley 17.622), SEN structure, national accounts, CPI, labour force (EPH), monthly activity (EMAE), poverty lines (CBA/CBT), population census, BCRA external/monetary anchors, Mercosur (static international). Definition locked before research.
meta.strategy_note: Follows NEXT-COUNTRY-STRATEGY.md: logs first, definition locked, INDEC catalogue first, hierarchy template ready for later batches.

candidates.title: Ley Nº 17.622 — Creación del Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC) y del Sistema Estadístico Nacional
candidates.publisher: Poder Ejecutivo Nacional / Congreso de la Nación Argentina
candidates.description: Foundational 1968 statute that creates INDEC, organises the Sistema Estadístico Nacional (SEN) under the principle of normative centralisation and executive decentralisation, and assigns INDEC direction of all official statistics in the national territory. Still the core legal basis for official statistics (with Decree 3110/70 and later complementary norms).
referenced_by: INDEC institutional pages and methodological documents
Resolución 130/2025 and Programa Anual de Trabajo references to the legal framework
OECD and IMF assessments of the Argentine statistical system
Every major INDEC programme methodology that cites the SEN legal basis
candidates.notes:
Prime static + recurring-citation node — exact analogue of Mexico’s LSNIEG.

Contextual framing from the law itself and later references:
Ley 17.622 establishes that INDEC shall ‘unificar la orientación y ejercer la dirección superior de todas las actividades estadísticas oficiales que se realicen en el territorio de la Nación’ and ‘estructurar, mediante la articulación y coordinación de los servicios estadísticos nacionales, provinciales y municipales, el Sistema Estadístico Nacional… de acuerdo con el principio de centralización normativa y descentralización ejecutiva.’

Subsequent instruments (Decree 3110/70, Resolución 130/2025, Programa Anual de Trabajo) and international assessments continuously cite this statute as the legal foundation. No independent publication cadence is required; the recurring institutional citation satisfies the expanded node definition.

candidates.title: Sistema Estadístico Nacional (SEN) / National Statistical System of Argentina
candidates.description: The organised set of statistical services of national, provincial and municipal bodies that produce official statistics. Coordinated by INDEC under normative centralisation and executive decentralisation. Each province has a Dirección Provincial de Estadística (DPE).
referenced_by: Relevamiento del Sistema Estadístico Nacional publications
candidates.notes: Institutional framework node. Continuously referenced as the organisational architecture within which INDEC and the DPEs operate. Static in the sense that it is not a periodic statistical release, but load-bearing and recurringly cited.

candidates.title: Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales (SCN) / National Accounts of Argentina
candidates.publisher: INDEC — Dirección Nacional de Cuentas Nacionales
candidates.description: Full national-accounts system producing GDP (production, expenditure, income), Supply and Use Tables (COU), institutional sector accounts, generation of income, and related aggregates. Current base year 2004 (with ongoing revision work). Quarterly and annual releases.
candidates.notes: Core macroeconomic statistical system. Methodological publications document the base-2004 estimation procedures and the use of sources such as SIPA and EPH microdata. Satellite accounts (culture, etc.) are explicitly made compatible with the SCN revision.

candidates.title: Estimador Mensual de Actividad Económica (EMAE) / Monthly Estimator of Economic Activity
candidates.description: Monthly volume indicator of economic activity that provides an early signal of GDP movements. Published with original, seasonally adjusted and trend-cycle series.
candidates.notes: Principal high-frequency activity indicator. Regularly cited in INDEC Informa and in BCRA / market analysis as the monthly proxy for GDP. May 2026 release showed +0.2% year-on-year (seasonally adjusted) and −0.5% month-on-month (original).

candidates.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) / Consumer Price Index
candidates.publisher: INDEC — Dirección Nacional de Estadísticas de Precios
candidates.description: National consumer price index measuring monthly changes in the prices of a representative basket of goods and services consumed by urban households. Published for Total Nacional and major regions (GBA, Pampeana, Noreste, Noroeste, Cuyo, Patagonia). Core, seasonal and regulated breakdowns also released.
candidates.notes: Flagship price statistic. July 2026: +2.1% month-on-month, +19.3% year-to-date. Disseminated within 8–10 working days after month-end (SDDS). Direct input into the valorization of the Canasta Básica Alimentaria and Canasta Básica Total used for poverty lines.

candidates.title: Sistema de Índices de Precios Mayoristas (SIPM) — IPIM, IPIB, IPP
candidates.description: Wholesale price system comprising the Índice de Precios Internos al por Mayor (IPIM), Índice de Precios Internos Básicos al por Mayor (IPIB) and Índice de Precios Básicos del Productor (IPP). Monthly.
candidates.notes: Complements the IPC on the producer/wholesale side. Used in national-accounts deflation and industrial analysis.

candidates.title: Encuesta Permanente de Hogares (EPH) / Permanent Household Survey
candidates.description: Continuous household survey that is the primary source for labour-market indicators (activity, employment, unemployment, underemployment, informality) and for income-based poverty measurement in 31 urban agglomerations. Microdata released regularly.
candidates.notes: Central social and labour survey. Q1 2026: activity rate 48.6%, employment rate 44.8%, unemployment rate 7.8%. Also the source for the official poverty and indigency incidence figures published each semester. Extended total-urban version exists.

candidates.title: Incidencia de la pobreza y la indigencia (líneas CBA / CBT)
candidates.description: Official income-poverty and indigency (extreme poverty) rates for the 31 EPH urban agglomerations. Calculated by comparing household income with the Canasta Básica Alimentaria (CBA = indigency line) and Canasta Básica Total (CBT = poverty line). Published twice yearly.
candidates.notes: Headline social indicator. Second semester 2025: 21.0% of households / 28.2% of persons below the poverty line; 4.8% of households / 6.3% of persons below the indigency line (31 agglomerations). Values of CBA and CBT are updated monthly with the IPC.

candidates.title: Canasta Básica Alimentaria (CBA) y Canasta Básica Total (CBT) / Basic Food Basket and Total Basic Basket
candidates.description: Monthly monetary values of the food basket (indigency line) and the total basic basket (poverty line) for an adult-equivalent and for reference households, by region. Updated with the IPC.
candidates.notes: Direct input into the poverty measurement. July 2026: CBT for a reference household of four required more than $1.56 million to stay above the poverty line. Regional series published (GBA, etc.).

candidates.title: Censo Nacional de Población, Hogares y Viviendas / National Population, Household and Housing Census
candidates.description: Decennial (most recent 2022) census of population, households and dwellings. Provides the structural demographic and housing baseline and sampling frames for household surveys.
candidates.notes: Foundational demographic product. 2022 census results and REDATAM databases are the reference for population structure, housing characteristics and small-area estimation. Continuously cited by EPH design, poverty analysis and provincial statistical offices.

candidates.title: Balanza de Pagos / Balance of Payments (BCRA)
candidates.publisher: Banco Central de la República Argentina (BCRA)
candidates.description: Quarterly balance-of-payments statistics compiled by the central bank. Covers current account, capital account, financial account and reserve assets.
candidates.notes: Core external-accounts product. Complements INDEC merchandise-trade and national-accounts data. Regular press releases give the quarterly aggregates and ratios to GDP.

candidates.title: Reservas Internacionales del BCRA / International Reserves
candidates.publisher: Banco Central de la República Argentina (BCRA)
candidates.description: Stock of international reserves held by the BCRA. Published at high frequency (daily/weekly/monthly) and analysed in the Informe Monetario Mensual.
candidates.notes: Key external-vulnerability and monetary-policy indicator. Appears in the weekly/monthly monetary reports and in the balance-of-payments financial account (change in reserve assets).

candidates.title: Base monetaria y agregados monetarios / Monetary base and monetary aggregates
candidates.publisher: Banco Central de la República Argentina (BCRA)
candidates.description: Regular statistics of the monetary base and broader monetary aggregates (M2, M3, etc.) published by the BCRA and analysed in the Informe Monetario Mensual.
candidates.notes: Core monetary statistics. The monthly monetary report tracks real and seasonally adjusted movements, factors of expansion/contraction, and ratios to GDP.

candidates.title: Tratado de Asunción / Mercado Común del Sur (MERCOSUR)
candidates.publisher: Estados Parte del MERCOSUR (Argentina, Brasil, Paraguay, Uruguay, etc.)
candidates.description: Foundational 1991 treaty establishing the Southern Common Market. Static legal instrument governing preferential trade, common external tariff aspirations and regional integration. Continuously cited in Argentine trade statistics, BCRA analysis and policy documents.
referenced_by: BCRA and Ministry of Economy reports on regional trade shares
REES (Reunión Especializada de Estadísticas del Mercosur) coordinated statistical work
candidates.notes:
Prime international static + recurring-citation node — analogue of Mexico’s T-MEC.

Contextual framing: the Treaty of Asunción (23 March 1991) created MERCOSUR with the objectives of free circulation of goods and services, a common external commercial policy, and coordination of sectoral policies. Thirty-five years on it remains the institutional framework for a large share of Argentina’s regional trade (partner countries accounted for roughly 19% of Argentine exports and 29% of imports in recent figures). INDEC participates in the Reunión Especializada de Estadísticas del Mercosur (REES). No separate ‘MERCOSUR statistical yearbook’ is required for the instrument to qualify; the recurring citation in trade and integration analysis is sufficient under the expanded node definition.

proposed_edges.basis: National accounts are produced by INDEC under the legal mandate and SEN architecture established by Ley 17.622.
EPH is an official statistical operation of the SEN coordinated by INDEC under the foundational law.
Poverty and indigency incidence are calculated from EPH household income data.
Poverty/indigency status is determined by comparing household income with the CBA and CBT values.
CBA and CBT monetary values are updated monthly with the IPC.
EMAE is the monthly estimator aligned with the national-accounts framework.
Regional trade flows under MERCOSUR preferences are a recurring analytical dimension of the balance of payments and external-sector reports.
